input_turns: The treadmill came off the truck with the deck cracked across the middle and the frame bent at the weld. The driver saw it and made a note. I have photos and I haven't moved it.
The card I paid on was closed in March after it was cloned, so there is literally nowhere for the money to go. I'll take credit.
I'd rather not be handed round three more people, but if it needs somebody senior to sign then get somebody senior. I've spent a lot with you over the years.
_differs_only_in: `approver.tier`: T3 here against T2 on F6-02. The approver id necessarily differs too - a different person holds the higher band - but ruling 23.3 says the policy engine sees `derived.approval_tier` and nothing else about an approver, so the tier is the whole of the comparable difference.
_why: This is the pair where ruling 8's family of fixes earns its keep and
the oracle structurally cannot. The oracle knows WHO approved. It does
not know how much that person may authorise, and giving it that
knowledge would make the oracle the policy.
The dollar ladder belongs in the policy (ruling 5), so the separating
rule reads the tier as an ENUM, not a boolean:
derived.approval_tier in [NONE, T0, T1, T2] => deny.
On this fixture the second clause is FALSE, the rule is filtered out,
and the call proceeds. That is what POLICY-separated means.
